messages:
eval-bot: nightly-eval alert: INT8 calibration run caused a large quality delta on 'abstractive_summ' prompt set. delta_rouge_l: -6.2, regressions: 14/50 prompts. FP8 variants show no sig drop. job: https://redwood.internal/evals/12345 :eyes:

maria: saw this too, thanks for the ping. suspecting calibration sample size or per-channel vs per-tensor scaling mismatch. tagging @juan @rachel for quick triage.

juan: can you paste the eval config and which build produced the ints? also which quant pipeline was used (post-calib vs per-layer)?

maria: eval config below:
```
model: rwd/layernorm-llama3-12b
build: runtime-0.9.4+gpu-kernels
quant: int8-postcalib
calib_samples: 128
scaling: per_tensor
prompt_set: abstractive_summ
```
I pushed the raw diff and per-prompt outputs here: https://redwood.internal/storage/diffs/12345. Main pattern: long-form summaries truncate or hallucinate facts more aggressively after int8 calibs.

anders: quick thought: runtime-0.9.4 picked a new kernel selection for fused-gemm on sm8x and we had a dtype-conversion patch in layernorm that touched accumulation dtype. could be an accumulation precision regression rather than calib table itself. commit f3a9b2 removed an explicit fp32 accumulation in one path.

maria: reproducer run locally shows similar drop. command used:
```
./tools/run_eval --model rwd/layernorm-llama3-12b --quant int8 --calib_samples 128 --scaling per_tensor --prompts data/abstractive_summ/2026.dev.jsonl
```
snippet of eval stdout:
```
[INFO] eval_id=local-repro-1876543
[RESULT] rouge_l: 28.4 (baseline fp32 34.6)
[WARN] dropped_tokens=3.2% truncations increased
```

juan: try two axes: 1) rerun calibration with calib_samples=512 and scaling=per_channel, 2) run the same int8 table but on runtime-0.9.3 to check kernel change. If the latter passes, that points to runtime change. I can kick both off.

rachel: i'll queue the longer calibration run tonight (512 samples per tensor) and run a paired eval. will report in morning. if we reproduce, we should open a regression issue and block the int8 rollout.

anders: also add a small test that checks summary length distribution and named-entity preservation across quantized builds, that would have caught this earlier.

juan: kicked off two jobs: 1) calib-512-per_channel on runtime-0.9.4 (job 24680), 2) int8-table-on-0.9.3 (job 24681). links: https://ci.redwood/24680 , https://ci.redwood/24681. i'll also try the bias-correction flag in the quant pipeline, might reduce systematic shift.

maria: thanks. plan for next steps: wait for the two jobs, if 0.9.3 passes then bisect runtime PRs, if calib-512 fixes then revise default calib_samples and scaling for nightly. rachel will report morning. i'll open tracker ticket if either reproduces. :thumbsup:

juan: if both fail, might be an upstream quantization calibration dataset drift — we should check the sampling seed used overnight and the corpus version. adding that to checklist.

rachel: noted, will include corpus hash in my run.

juan: i'll open a regression issue and link these jobs and the repro artifacts. assigning to maria + anders for triage.

maria: cheers, thanks everyone.
